inline.s: Moreover, Sariputra, seeing this great causal occasion of benefit and bliss, I speak these words of truth: if any good man or good woman of pure faith should hear this name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, with its inconceivable merit and virtue, and this pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, they should all believe and accept it, make the vow, and practice as taught, that they may be born in that Buddha-land.

Therefore, Sariputra, seeing this great causal occasion of benefit and bliss, I speak sincerely and truthfully: if any good man or good woman of pure faith can hear this name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, with its inconceivable merit and virtue, and this pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, they should all believe and accept it, make the vow, and practice as taught, that they may be born in that Buddha-land.
[Faith and acceptance]
This sutra states:
“The Buddhas of the ten directions speak words of truth:
you beings should all
believe and accept
this ‘praise of the inconceivable merits and virtue of the Buddha-land, the dharma received and protected by all Buddhas
dharma’.”
” [Making the vow] This sutra states: “Sariputra, if beings, hearing of that Western pure Buddha-land of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, adorned with immeasurable merits and virtues,
should all make the vow to be born in that Buddha-land
[All should believe, accept, and make the vow, practice as taught, and be born in that Buddha-land]

Here the World-honored One sets forth faith, vow, and practice with the utmost clarity: faith is believing and accepting this sutra (the dharma received and protected by all Buddhas); vow is resolving to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; practice is cultivating as taught — keeping the mind fixed and unconfused. In this way one can be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

inline.s: The praise of the Buddhas of the ten directions,
of course also includes the praise of Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. From this one can see how important this sutra is to the Pure Land school!

[Ganga (jìng jiā)]a transliteration of the Sanskrit word for the Ganges River. [Broad and long tongue]one of the thirty-two marks of the Buddha: the Buddha’s tongue is broad and long, soft, red, and thin, able to cover the face up to the hairline. Since the tongue is thus, his speech is necessarily truthful. [Three-thousand-great-thousand world system]that is, one great-thousand world system, the region over which a single Buddha teaches. A single Mount Sumeru together with the four great continents is called a small world; a thousand small worlds form a small-thousand world; a thousand small-thousand worlds form a medium-thousand world; a thousand medium-thousand worlds form a great-thousand world. Because it is counted as a thousand three times, a great-thousand world is also called a three-thousand-great-thousand world system. [Mount Sumeru]rendered in Chinese as the Supreme Mountain, the center of a small world. This mountain is made of the four treasures of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal; no other mountain can match its height, so it is the king of mountains. [The four great continents]Around Mount Sumeru are four great continents: the East is Purvavideha, the South is Jambudvipa (the world in which we live is on this continent), the West is Godaniya, and the North is Uttarakuru.

blocks.text: 5. Received and Protected by All Buddhas

inline.s: The previous chapter, “The Buddhas of the Ten Directions Praise,” and this chapter, “Received and Protected by All Buddhas,” together prove
that the Sutra of the Praise of the Pure Land Buddha-land, Received and Protected, is
(of course including also Amitabha Buddha)
praised by the Buddhas and
(of course including also Amitabha Buddha)

received and protected by the Buddhas. In other words, the Sutra of the Praise of the Pure Land Buddha-land, Received and Protected, is spoken by the golden mouth of our original teacher, Sakyamuni Buddha, and is the dharma praised and received-protected by Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Therefore this sutra is the fundamental basis for the study and practice of the Pure Land school. Those who recite the Buddha’s name should practice as taught and be born in that Buddha-land.

Moreover, Sariputra, why is this sutra named “Praise of the Inconceivable Merits and Virtue of the Buddha-land, the Dharma Received and Protected by All Buddhas”? Sariputra, because in this sutra the merits and virtues of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life are proclaimed and praised, and the World-honored Buddhas of the ten directions, wishing by skillful means to bring benefit and bliss to all beings, each dwelling in his own land, display great miraculous transformations and speak words of truth, urging all beings to believe and accept this dharma. Therefore this sutra is named “Praise of the Inconceivable Merits and Virtue of the Buddha-land, the Dharma Received and Protected by All Buddhas.”

Then, Sariputra, for what reason is this sutra named “Praise of the Inconceivable Merits and Virtue of the Buddha-land, the Dharma Received and Protected by All Buddhas”? Sariputra, because in this sutra the merits and virtues of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life are proclaimed and praised, together with the World-honored Buddhas of the ten directions (of course also including Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss), who, wishing by skillful means to bring benefit and bliss to all beings, each dwelling in his own land, display great miraculous transformations and speak sincerely and earnestly, urging all beings to believe and accept this dharma. Therefore this sutra is named “Praise of the Inconceivable Merits and Virtue of the Buddha-land, the Dharma Received and Protected by All Buddhas”.

blocks.text: (1) Do Not Give Rise to Doubt

inline.s: Moreover, Sariputra, if any good man or good woman — whether they have already heard, or shall hear, or now hear this sutra — on hearing it should give rise to deep faith and understanding. Having given rise to faith and understanding, they will certainly be received and protected by the World-honored Buddhas who dwell in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers. Those who practice as taught will without exception be irrevocable from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and will without exception be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.

Moreover, Sariputra, if any good man or good woman — whether they have already made the vow, shall make the vow, or now make the vow toward the merits and adornments of the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life — they will certainly be received and protected by the World-honored Buddhas who dwell in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers. Those who practice as taught will without exception be irrevocable from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and will without exception be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.

Therefore, Sariputra, if any good man or good woman — whether they have already made the vow, shall make the vow, or now make the vow toward the merits and adornments of the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life — they will surely be received and protected by the World-honored Buddhas who dwell in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers. Those who practice as taught will without exception be irrevocable from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and will without exception be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.

Therefore, Sariputra, if any good man or good woman of pure faith, all should, with deep faith and understanding toward the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, make the vow to be reborn there, and not indulge in laxness.

Therefore, Sariputra, if any good man or good woman of pure faith, all should, with deep faith and understanding toward the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, make the vow to be reborn there and by no means indulge in lax self-indulgence;

Moreover, Sariputra, just as I now proclaim and praise, together with all the Buddhas, the inconceivable merits and virtues of the Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, so the World-honored Buddhas of the ten directions also praise my inconceivable, boundless merits and virtues, all saying: Most rare and wonderful! Sakyamuni the Still, Sakya the Dharma-King, the Tathagata, the Worthy One, the Fully Enlightened One, Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, the Well-Gone One, Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Tamer, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Buddha the World-honored One — that he should have been able, in this endurance world (Saha world), in the evil age of the five defilements, namely the defilement of the age, the defilement of beings, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of views, the defilement of life, to attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi therein, and for the sake of benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings through skillful means, to speak this dharma that is most difficult to believe in this world.

Moreover, Sariputra, just as I now proclaim and praise, together with all the Buddhas, the inconceivable merits and virtues of the Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, so the World-honored Buddhas of the ten directions also praise my inconceivable, boundless merits and virtues, all saying: Most rare and wonderful! Sakyamuni the Dharma-King, the Tathagata, the Worthy One, the Fully Enlightened One, Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, the Well-Gone One, Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Tamer, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Buddha the World-honored One — that he should have been able, in this Saha world, in the evil age of the five defilements (the defilement of the age, the defilement of beings, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of views, the defilement of life), to attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi therein, and for the sake of benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings through skillful means, to speak this dharma that is most difficult to believe in this world.

[Sakyamuni the Still]The two characters muni in Sakyamuni mean stillness. [Dharma-King]The Buddha is the lord of the Dharma-door, able to teach beings freely, and is therefore called Dharma-King. [Tamer]That is the Tamer of Men mentioned in the earlier notes. [The five defilements]First, the defilement of the age: the era encounters misfortune and disasters arise again and again; second, the defilement of afflictions: the minds of people are filled with greed, anger, and delusion; third, the defilement of beings (also called the defilement of beings): beings are of lowly capacity, with much suffering and little joy; fourth, the defilement of views: wrong views prevail and thought is in disorder; fifth, the defilement of life: beings receive retribution for evil karma, their bodies and minds are worn out, and their life-span is short. [The dharma most difficult to believe in the world]The Land of Ultimate Bliss is so supremely wondrous that one need only keep the mind fixed and unconfused to be reborn there by relying on the Buddha’s power and attain Buddhahood in a single lifetime. But how many people in the world truly believe and practice as taught? Therefore this is the dharma most difficult to believe in the world.

Therefore, Sariputra, know that I now, in this defiled endurance world, in the evil age of the five defilements, have attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings through skillful means, have spoken this dharma that is most difficult to believe in this world — most rare, wonderful, and inconceivable.

Therefore, Sariputra, know that I now, in this defiled endurance world, the Saha world, in the evil age of the five defilements, have attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings through skillful means, have spoken this dharma that is most difficult to believe in this world — most rare, wonderful, and inconceivable.

Moreover, Sariputra, in this defiled endurance world, in the evil age of the five defilements, if any good man or good woman of pure faith should hear this dharma, most difficult to believe in all the world, and can give rise to faith and understanding, receive it, uphold it, proclaim it, and practice as instructed — know that such a person is most rare, and has planted roots of goodness in the presence of countless Buddhas. At the end of life such a person will surely be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, enjoying the manifold merits and adornments of that pure Buddha-land and the joy of the Great Dharma; day and night, throughout the six periods, drawing near to and making offerings to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life; traveling through the ten directions and making offerings to all the Buddhas. In the presence of each Buddha, hearing the Dharma and receiving the prophecy, their stores of merit and wisdom will quickly be perfected, and they will quickly realize the unexcelled right and equal enlightenment.

Therefore, Sariputra, in this defiled endurance world, the Saha world, in the evil age of the five defilements, if any good man or good woman of pure faith should hear this Pure Land dharma, most difficult to believe in all the world, and can give rise to faith and understanding, receive it, uphold it, proclaim it, and practice as instructed — know that such a person is most rare, and has planted roots of goodness in the presence of countless Buddhas. At the end of life such a person will surely be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, enjoying the manifold merits and adornments of that pure Buddha-land and the joy of the Great Dharma; day and night, throughout the six periods, drawing near to and making offerings to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life; traveling through the ten directions and making offerings to all the Buddhas. In the presence of each Buddha, hearing the Dharma and receiving the prophecy, their stores of merit and wisdom will quickly be perfected, and they will quickly realize the unexcelled right and equal enlightenment.

[Receiving the prophecy]To receive from a Buddha the prediction that one will in the future certainly become a Buddha. [Merit and wisdom as provisions]The Buddha is complete in both merit and wisdom; therefore merit and wisdom are the provisions for attaining Buddhahood. [Provisions]Resources are the wealth, and provisions the food. Practicing the path is like a long journey: one must have the provisions of merit and wisdom in order to reach the destination. For those who recite the Buddha’s name and seek rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, it is necessary to have the three provisions of faith, vow, and practice.

At that time, when the Bhagavat had spoken this sutra, the Venerable Sariputra and the other great sravakas, together with the assemblies of bodhisattva mahasattvas, and immeasurable devas, humans, asuras, and others, all the great multitude, hearing what the Buddha had said, were filled with great joy, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
At this

time the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra. The Venerable Sariputra and the other great sravakas, together with the assemblies of bodhisattva mahasattvas, and immeasurable devas, humans, asuras, and others, all the great multitude, hearing what the Buddha had said, were filled with great joy, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
